newsitem.title: CHINA: KAL gets hold rating from Salomon.
newsitem.headline: KAL gets hold rating from Salomon.

text.p: Salomon Brothers is forecasting growth in dedicated cargo capacity at Korean Airlines of close to 11 percent compounded over 1997-2000 as a result of the South Korean flag carrier's drive to become the world's leading air cargo carrier.
The investment bankers, in an airline research report accompanying a stock Hold rating, said KAL is heading for financial recovery but is expected to make another loss this year.

Earnings at South Korea's largest domestic and international flag carrier slumped to a 210 billion Won ($235.6 million) loss in 1996 due to a weak local currency and slowing economy which reduced passenger traffic growth, the report said. Combined with tough competitive pressure, yields fell by 4 percent over 1995's level.
Capacity, which has been rising annually by 14.2 percent between 1991 and 1996, is forecast to slow to 8 percent in 1997 before rising to 12 percent in 1998.

"In 1997, we expect another loss, although smaller than that seen in 1996 as further depreciation in the currency, slower economic growth and intense competition again combine to limit revenue growth."
In 1998, KAL's prospects should improve, pushing the company back into profit. Gains from aircraft sales should boost earnings further," the report said.

Issuing a Hold rating, Salomon said it had a "positive" outlook on the Korean share market and believed KAL's return to profit should allow the stock to rally in line with the market. Salomon's 12-month target price is 23,500 Won.

The report said KAL's domestic and international cargo business recorded compounded annual growth of 40.5 percent and 12.2 percent respectively over the five years to 1996 while total available cargo capacity rose by 13.7 percent.

As KAL aims to become the world's number-one cargo airline, Salomon said aside from currency pressures, competition will remain tough both from South Korea's rapidly expanding second carrier, Asiana Airlines, and other Asian rivals.

Despite that, Salomon said it expects KAL's cargo operations to remain a major focus of growth as the airline's cargo fleet expands from 19 aircraft at the end of last year to 27 by the end of 2000. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 $ = 891.5 South Korean Won)
